overview: This Senate resolution named March 21, 2026, the first Saturday after the start of spring, as 'National Day of Play' and supports marking that day every year. It points to concerns about loneliness, too little physical activity, and heavy screen time, and describes how play helps children's development and relieves stress for people of all ages. The resolution encourages people to put down their electronics and play. It does not create a federal holiday. The Senate approved it on March 22, 2026.
for: Supporters say a yearly day of play is a simple way to encourage families and communities to spend time together away from screens and be more active.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending.
